title: Agent 64: Spies Never Die review – licence to kill time like the 90s never ended
excerpt: This GoldenEye 007-styled retro shooter is an agreeable set of straightahead shooting missions that hark back to a simpler time, with simpler controls
content_html:
With 007 First Light, 2026 has already given us the best James Bond game in more than three decades, since the release of Rare’s N64 classic GoldenEye 007. But what about those players whose loyalties lie not with the super-spy himself but the particulars of that 90s interpretation of his adventures?

Enter Agent 64: Spies Never Die. Made almost entirely by a single developer (who goes by the very cloak-and-dagger alias Replicant D6), its production values couldn’t be much further from the blockbuster First Light. There’s no voice acting, with all dialogue instead delivered via subtitles, while each location on your globe-trotting adventure is depicted by a repeating texture wallpapered over scenery so blocky you can count the individual polygons.

In lieu of any high-budget flash, Agent 64’s big special effect is nostalgia. From the title onwards, this retro shooter is one long homage to GoldenEye, and to its un-Bonded successor, 2000’s Perfect Dark.

Enemies have pinched facial features – a result of taking photographs of real people’s faces and wrapping them around diamond-shaped heads – and roll acrobatically from behind cover to take their next potshot, just as they used to. And yes, there’s a Big Head mode that swells those diamonds into enormous target-practice balloons.

Less explicably, Agent 64 retains the slightly strange control scheme of its inspirations, even though it doesn’t have to work around the (iconic but unwieldy) N64 pad that made it a necessity. You can pull a trigger for a zoomed-in precision aim, but somehow this is even fiddlier to steer with a modern analogue stick or mouse than it was back then. The first level features a pair of locks you must manually shoot; they remain the game’s toughest bosses.

Better by far to just run and gun, letting the generous auto-aim do its thing. OK, the target your gun seeks out might not always be the one you expected, or wanted, but playing this way unlocks a hectic pace of action that – nostalgic warmth aside – is Agent 64’s greatest asset.

It’s essential to the joys of split-screen deathmatch multiplayer, which generates the same kind of giggly fun that filled so many late 90s living rooms, especially once the match rules have been tweaked to allow only proximity mines or melee judo chops. (You can play online, but this is so counter to the elbows-on-the-sofa appeal of the thing that I never actually attempt it.)

Meanwhile, the story mode (which can be played solo or co-op with a partner) is so in hock to games of old that it ignores the subsequent 30 years of level-design knowhow. The number of dead ends and looping identical corridors can be infuriating, especially since dying means starting over from the beginning, but this is offset by the briskness of the missions. Each can be finished in less than five minutes, at which point the game will challenge you with a “par time” that often comes in under two minutes.

As you revisit these levels, trying to shave off vital seconds, their layouts begin to make much more sense. These are obstacle courses, really, where enemies aren’t so much a threat as they are something to be hurdled – or better yet, avoided. On top of this, Agent 64 piles hidden collectibles and challenge variants that recycle the levels in yet more ways, and their size makes them incredibly moreish.

The fantasy on offer here isn’t really being James Bond. It’s being young again, with one illicitly acquired copy of GoldenEye to last you the summer and all the time in the world to pick the cartridge clean. For all its rough edges, that’s a mission Agent 64 pulls off with aplomb.

  • Agent 64: Spies Never Die is out now, £19.64

content_html_zh:
自 Rare 的 N64 经典《黄金眼 007》发行以来，《007 曙光 2026》已经为我们带来了三十多年来最好的詹姆斯·邦德游戏。 但那些忠诚于超级间谍本人而不是 90 年代对其冒险经历的细节的玩家呢？

《特工 64：间谍不死》登场。 它几乎完全由一个开发者（他的别名 Replicant D6）制作，它的制作价值与轰动一时的《First Light》相差无几。 没有配音，所有对话都通过字幕传递，而环球旅行冒险中的每个地点都由重复的纹理描绘，风景上布满了壁纸，如此块状，你可以数出各个多边形。

与任何高预算的闪光灯不同，《64 号特工》最大的特效是怀旧。 从标题开始，这款复古射击游戏就是对 GoldenEye 及其非 Bonded 继任者 2000 年的 Perfect Dark 的长期致敬。

敌人会捏住面部特征——这是拍摄真人面部照片并将其包裹在菱形头部的结果——然后像以前一样从掩体后面巧妙地翻滚来拍摄下一次射击。 是的，有一个大头模式可以将这些钻石膨胀成巨大的目标练习气球。

更难以解释的是，Agent 64 保留了其灵感中略显奇怪的控制方案，尽管它不必围绕（标志性但笨重的）N64 键盘进行工作，而 N64 键盘使其成为必需品。 你可以扣动扳机来进行放大的精确瞄准，但不知何故，用现代的模拟摇杆或鼠标来操纵比以前更加繁琐。 第一关有一对锁，你必须手动射击；他们仍然是游戏中最难对付的老板。

到目前为止，最好只是边跑边开枪，让慷慨的自动瞄准发挥作用。 好吧，你的枪寻找的目标可能并不总是你所期望或想要的目标，但以这种方式玩可以解锁紧张的行动节奏，除了怀旧的温暖之外，这也是《64 号特工》最大的资产。

这对于分屏死亡竞赛多人游戏的乐趣至关重要，它会产生与许多 90 年代末的客厅相同的咯咯笑的乐趣，尤其是当比赛规则被调整为只允许近距离地雷或近战柔道斩时。 （你可以在线玩，但这与把肘部放在沙发上的吸引力背道而驰，所以我从未真正尝试过。）

与此同时，故事模式（可以单人玩，也可以与伙伴合作）过于传统的游戏，以至于忽略了随后 30 年的关卡设计技巧。 死胡同和循环相同走廊的数量可能会令人恼火，特别是因为死亡意味着从头开始，但这被任务的敏捷性所抵消。 每个任务都可以在五分钟内完成，此时游戏将向您发起“标准时间”的挑战，该“标准时间”通常会在两分钟内完成。

当你重新审视这些关卡，试图缩短重要的时间时，它们的布局开始变得更有意义。 实际上，这些都是障碍训练场，在这里，敌人与其说是威胁，不如说是需要跨越的东西——或者更好的是，避免它们。 除此之外，《Agent 64》还堆放了隐藏的收藏品和挑战变体，以更多方式循环利用关卡，而且它们的大小让它们变得异常可爱。

这里提供的幻想并不是真正的詹姆斯·邦德。 它又年轻了，一本非法获得的《黄金眼》可以让你度过整个夏天，并在世界上所有的时间里把墨盒都清理干净。 尽管存在诸多困难，但《64 号特工》却沉着地完成了这项任务。

  • 《特工 64：间谍永不死》现已发售，售价 19.64 英镑
